o: Identify clock speed, cache size and number of cores as the three CPU performance factors.
Explain how changing each factor can affect CPU performance.
Compare two CPUs using evidence from their specifications.
refs: L018 / L010 · image size and compression
r: What is stored by the Program Counter (PC), and what is held in the Memory Data Register (MDR)?
PC: address of the next instruction to be fetched. MDR: the data or instruction currently being transferred to/from memory. Both are registers.
Identify one job of the ALU and one job of the Control Unit.
ALU: arithmetic and logical operations. Control Unit: decodes instructions and coordinates/controls CPU activity.
Convert 4 KB to bytes using the decimal convention 1 KB = 1,000 bytes.
A 120 × 80 pixel image uses 8-bit colour depth. Calculate the uncompressed pixel-data size in bytes. Why should a source-code file use lossless rather than lossy compression?
120 × 80 = 9,600 pixels. × 8 = 76,800 bits. ÷ 8 = 9,600 bytes. Lossless is required to restore the original source code exactly.
c: Clock speed is measured in hertz (Hz). A higher clock speed means the CPU carries out more clock cycles each second, so it can generally process instructions faster.
Cache is small, fast memory used to store frequently used data and instructions. A larger cache can reduce the need to fetch them from slower main memory (RAM), improving performance.
A core processes instructions. A processor with more cores can process more tasks at the same time, which can improve performance when several programs are running.

Look at all three factors: clock speed, cache size and number of cores. For example, one CPU may have a higher clock speed while another has more cores and a larger cache. Explain which factors matter for the stated task.

m.q: Two school computers have different processors. CPU A: 3.2 GHz, 2 cores, 4 MB cache. CPU B: 2.8 GHz, 4 cores, 8 MB cache. Explain TWO reasons CPU B may be more suitable when several programs are open. [4 marks]
st: Read the table. CPU A has the higher clock speed; CPU B has more cores and a larger cache. The question is about running several programs.
First reason: CPU B has four cores rather than two [1]. More cores can process more tasks at the same time, improving multitasking [1].
Second reason: CPU B has 8 MB cache rather than 4 MB [1]. More frequently used data and instructions can be accessed quickly, reducing slower RAM access [1].

Check the command word 'explain': each reason must link a CPU characteristic to an improvement. CPU A's higher clock speed is a valid comparison, but we cannot guarantee which CPU is faster in every task.

w: CPU A runs at 3.2 GHz and CPU B at 2.8 GHz. Which has the higher clock speed? Explain one possible performance advantage. [2 marks]
CPU A has the higher clock speed [1]. Its CPU performs more clock cycles each second, so it may process instructions faster [1].
A processor is upgraded from 4 MB of cache to 8 MB. Explain how this could improve performance. [2 marks]
A larger cache can hold more frequently used data and instructions [1], reducing slower accesses to RAM [1].
A school replaces a two-core CPU with a four-core CPU. How might this help when many programs are open? [2 marks]
More cores can process more tasks simultaneously [1], improving performance when the computer is running multiple programs [1].

k.q: Code First · Predict what this short OCR Exam Reference Language program displays. Then compare the clock speeds of two CPUs.
k.code:
clockA = 3.2
clockB = 2.8
if clockA > clockB then
    print("CPU A has a higher clock speed")
else
    print("CPU B has an equal or higher clock speed")
endif
p: Predict the exact line of output before running the program.
Change clockB to 3.6. What does the program display now?
Extend the program: add coresA = 2 and coresB = 4, then use another IF statement to display which CPU has more cores.
k.a:
Original output: CPU A has a higher clock speed

With clockB = 3.6, the output is: CPU B has an equal or higher clock speed

Complete extended OCR ERL example:
clockA = 3.2
clockB = 3.6
coresA = 2
coresB = 4
if clockA > clockB then
    print("CPU A has a higher clock speed")
else
    print("CPU B has an equal or higher clock speed")
endif
if coresA > coresB then
    print("CPU A has more cores")
else
    print("CPU B has at least as many cores")
endif

Expected output:
CPU B has an equal or higher clock speed
CPU B has at least as many cores

The program compares CPU specifications. It does not measure real-world performance.

e:
State the three characteristics of a CPU that affect performance. [3 marks]

Source: Original J277-style question based on OCR J277 1.1.2.
Clock speed [1]; cache size [1]; number of CPU cores [1].

A school compares two processors.
CPU A: 3.2 GHz, 2 cores, 4 MB cache.
CPU B: 2.8 GHz, 4 cores, 8 MB cache.
Explain why CPU B may be better for running several programs at the same time. [4 marks]

Source: Original J277-style application question based on OCR J277 1.1.2.

CPU B has four cores compared with two in CPU A [1], so it can process more tasks at the same time [1]. CPU B has a larger cache (8 MB rather than 4 MB) [1], so more frequently used data/instructions can be accessed quickly, reducing slower main-memory access [1]. CPU A has a higher clock speed, so CPU B cannot be guaranteed to win every task. This is a model mark allocation for original practice, not an official OCR mark scheme.

Explain how clock speed, cache size and the number of cores each affect CPU performance. [6 marks]

Source: Adapted from your Paper 1 revision booklet, section 1.1.2.

Clock speed: a higher clock speed provides more clock cycles each second [1], allowing the CPU to process instructions faster [1]. Cache size: a larger cache can store more frequently used data/instructions [1], reducing access to slower main memory [1]. Number of cores: more cores can process more tasks at the same time [1], improving multitasking/performance for tasks that can run in parallel [1]. This point-by-point allocation is a teaching model; assess extended answers against the relevant question criteria.
v: The number of clock cycles the CPU carries out per second, measured in hertz.
Unit of clock speed: one clock cycle per second.
Small, fast memory that stores frequently used data and instructions for the CPU.
Part of a CPU that processes instructions.
Processing more than one task at the same time using multiple CPU cores.
x: A processor with more cores can improve performance when several programs are running.
